b_confinement.tmp_write_detail: Playwright's artifacts dir is bound to os.tmpdir() at MODULE LOAD time (coreBundle.js:40647/44899/45997 ARTIFACTS_FOLDER/2/3 = join(os.tmpdir(),'playwright-artifacts-')). The driver requires playwright-core at line 140, BEFORE it sets process.env.TMPDIR at line 164, so the connectOverCDP legs create /tmp/playwright-artifacts-XXXXXX outside --scratch. Confirmed by a 50Hz /tmp watcher: 12 distinct /tmp/playwright-artifacts-* dirs appeared during one run (4 connectOverCDP arms x 3 reps); they are removed on clean exit, so a before/after diff shows none.
b_confinement.sigkill_detail: SIGKILL is not catchable, so the counter's own signal handler (which kills the driver group and sweeps --user-data-dir=<driverScratch>/) never runs; the detached driver group survives and the /tmp artifacts dir survives with it. The driver eventually self-cleans. Counter's declared setup control for SIGTERM passes; SIGKILL is not in the frozen control set.
b_confinement.sigterm_control_verdict: rc 2 setup, 'counter received SIGTERM; driver group killed, 0 chromium processes swept'

a_mode_laundering.design: Scratch lane = a copy of the frozen driver in which PUA/PLA/PLAB attach to a RUNNER-STARTED browser instead of launching one, keeping the recorded mode field 'launch'. The FROZEN counter is run --live against it with the COPY'S OWN sha as --expect-driver-sha256.

variants.name: v0-control
variants.desc: copy unmodified in behaviour (LAUNDER flag off)

variants.name: v1-pw-remote
variants.desc: Playwright arms attach via connectOverCDP(url) with isLocal ABSENT (remote)
variants.detail: child #s events [[input,false],[change,false]] expected [[input,true],[change,true]] - the remote (non-collocated) attach converts the local path to a payload, so the events become untrusted. The counter DETECTS the semantic change but only via the outcome check, never via the recorded mode field.

a_mode_laundering.proof_run: lane2: same laundering plus an extra receipt field ACTUAL_process_model recording what really happened. rc 0, verdict clean, 0 findings, 256 checks; the receipt shows all 24 legs actually runner_started_client_attached while 9 of them recorded mode='launch'.
a_mode_laundering.fabricated_browser_id_run: lane4: every leg's browserId replaced by randomUUID() while the real per-leg browsers stayed. rc 0, verdict clean, 0 findings - the counter's 'fresh-browser' check reads the recorded id string only.
a_mode_laundering.pin_binding: With the FROZEN pin, the laundered copy is rejected before it runs: rc 1, finding id 'driver-pin', 'driver not run'.
a_mode_laundering.conclusion: The counter binds the driver BYTES (sha256 pin) and the recorded receipt fields. It does NOT bind the process tree: the recorded mode field, the per-leg browser id, and the 'each leg gets its own browser' property are all driver-pin facts, exactly as declared limit 2 states. No counter check can distinguish 'client launched the browser' from 'runner started it and the client attached'.

transitive_deps.finding: The counter's 'libs' check hashes only the two TOP-LEVEL package directories (node_modules/puppeteer-core, node_modules/playwright-core) and the lockfile integrity string of those two. Tampering a transitive dependency (node_modules/ws/index.js, node_modules/typed-query-selector/package.json) leaves both tree hashes and both integrity strings byte-identical, so 'libs' stays clean. This is the already-declared r97 A1 item 6 limit (transitive packages are not bound), re-confirmed for r98, not a new gap.
